title: EUMETSAT releases Meteosat-12 imagery of Saharan dust over Mediterranean
excerpt: The geostationary weather satellite captured the dust cloud moving northeast across the sea on 25 August 2026.
bodyHtml:
EUMETSAT released imagery on October 9, 2026, showing a Saharan dust cloud moving northeast across the Mediterranean Sea. The data was captured on 25 August 2026 by the FCI instrument onboard the Meteosat-12 geostationary weather satellite.

The satellite, which operates 36,000km above the Earth, provides imagery for weather forecasting, climate monitoring, and the early detection of severe weather. According to EUMETSAT, Saharan dust particles are lifted by surface wind gusts and can be transported thousands of kilometres from their origin.

The agency noted that dust traveling over populated areas can reduce air quality and cause respiratory problems or flight delays. Over oceans, the dust can act as a fertiliser for phytoplankton, which are tiny marine plants that form the basis of the marine food chain.
